question_text: After seven netball matches, Kai has averaged 11 goals per game.

mark_breakdown.desc: Set up weighted mean equation $\frac{\sum xf}{\sum f} = 11$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The weighted mean formula is $\bar{x} = \frac{\sum x_i f_i}{\sum f_i}$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Forgetting to multiply each score by its corresponding frequency.

subparts.stem: How many goals will she need to score in the next game to improve her overall average to 12?
subparts.solution: Let $k$ be the number of goals that Kai will need to score in the next game. Since she averaged 11 goals in her first 7 games, her average after the next game $= \frac{7 \times 11 + k}{8} = \frac{k + 77}{8}$. For her overall average to improve to 12, we require $\frac{k + 77}{8} = 12 \implies k + 77 = 96 \implies k = 19$. So, Kai will need to score 19 goals in the next game to improve her overall average to 12.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The total sum after $n+1$ events is $(n \times \bar{x}_{old}) + x_{new} = (n+1) \times \bar{x}_{new}$.
step_by_step: Total goals needed after 8 games to have an average of 12 $= 8 \times 12 = 96$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Dividing by 7 instead of 8 for the new mean.
